name: POST /api/sla/policies - Define an SLA policy for a lead type
description:
Creates the SLA policy that decides how long a lead of a given type has for its first human response. Creating a row at the collection root, so it answers 201. Policies are matched FIRST-MATCH-WINS in ascending evaluation_order, deliberately mirroring how routing_rules are evaluated so an operator learns one precedence model rather than two: a policy with source_channel omitted is the catch-all. This is what makes 'different lead types get different SLAs' configurable rather than hard-coded - before this endpoint every lead got a flat 30-minute window regardless of channel, which is wrong in both directions (a live_chat prospect is waiting in the window right now, while a csv_import row is not). When NO policy matches a lead, routing falls back to the 30-minute default so a tenant that has configured nothing still gets a running clock. first_response_minutes is bounded to 1..10080 (one week): a zero-minute target would breach on arrival, and a target beyond a week is not an SLA anyone monitors. business_hours_only records the INTENT that the target should run on the tenant's business calendar; LeadFlow's local wall-clock fallback cannot honour it, and ProjexCloud sdk-sla applies it when the gateway is configured - the flag is stored either way so the policy does not have to be rewritten when the gateway is connected. Protected - SLA targets decide when somebody is judged late, so they are never publicly writable. QA: depends on register and login.

QA NOTE: one active policy per lead type per evaluation point is the rule. The suite runs against a database that already holds one, so the refusal is the assertion — a 201 would only pass on a database nobody had ever tested against.

testCases.name: A duplicate active policy for the same lead type and order is refused
Reject a zero-minute target that would breach on arrival

errorCases.when: name is missing or over 160 characters, source_channel is present but not one of the fourteen channels, first_response_minutes is absent or not an integer between 1 and 10080, business_hours_only is not a boolean, evaluation_order is not an integer between 0 and 100000, or is_active is not a boolean
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired

an active policy already exists for that source_channel at the same evaluation_order - two policies that tie would make the effective SLA depend on insertion order, which is not something an operator can reason about
